```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

tab <- function(name) {
  read_csv(file.path("results", "tables", name), show_col_types = FALSE)
}
```

# Executive result

This report describes an umbrella review of pre-shunt prediction and post-shunt response measurement in idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus. Review-level pooled estimates are not independent and were not meta-meta-analysed.

```{r key-numbers}
numbers <- tab("manuscript_numbers.csv")
kable(numbers[, c("metric", "formatted", "interpretation_status")], col.names = c("Metric", "Result", "Status"))
```

# Methodological quality

Primary quality analyses use the completed author consensus. Reviewer-specific results are retained only as transparency analyses and never replace the final adjudicated judgments.


Instrument validation is not treated as validation of an iNPH shunt-response threshold. MCID sources are counted only when explicitly specific to the response construct and population.

# Concordance, credibility, and reporting completeness

```{r concordance, out.width='100%'}
knitr::include_graphics("results/figures/figure_12_directional_concordance.png")
```

```{r credibility, out.width='100%'}
knitr::include_graphics("results/figures/figure_13_claim_credibility_profile.png")
```

The credibility profile is a transparent categorical framework developed for this review. It is not GRADE and it does not calculate a numerical score. Directional concordance is not interpreted as causal treatment-effect modification.

# Optional diagnostic meta-analysis

```{r dta-decision}
kable(tab("dta_meta_analysis_decision.csv"))
kable(tab("dta_meta_analysis_feasibility.csv"))
```

The current expected status is `NOT_READY_NO_PRIMARY_2X2_DATA`. This does not block the umbrella review. It indicates that an updated primary-study diagnostic-accuracy component would require separate data recovery, screening, extraction, cohort reconciliation, and risk-of-bias assessment.

# Interpretation

The evidence is more compatible with probabilistic, multimodal selection than solitary binary gatekeeping. Positive supplemental tests may increase confidence, whereas current review-level evidence does not establish any isolated negative test or absent marker as a validated stand-alone exclusion rule for clinically important shunt benefit. Prognostic association must not be interpreted as causal modification of the treatment effect.
